title: Retail Installment Contracts: State Credit of Late Charges Against the Hardship Extension Fee
content:
**Rule.** On a contract under Retail Installment Contracts, the late charges assessed on the installment due on the next due date, waived or not, are taken from the hardship extension fee according to the contract state:

- for a contract whose contract state is **GA, MS or LA** and whose contract date is on or after **1 July 2021** (2021-07-01), those late charges are taken from the fee **in full**;
- for a contract whose contract state is **TN, KY or AR**, they are taken **up to 5.00**;
- for every other contract nothing is taken.

**Which late charges.** Every late charge recorded against the installment due date equal to the contract's next due date at the effective date, including one later waived. Late charges recorded against earlier installment due dates are not taken.

| Contract | Late charges on the next-due installment | Amount taken from the fee |
|---|---|---|
| Louisiana, signed 2022 | 18.40 | 18.40 |
| Georgia, signed 30 June 2021 | 18.40 | nothing |
| Kentucky, any date | 18.40 | 5.00 |
| Arkansas, any date | 3.75 | 3.75 |
| Texas, any date | 18.40 | nothing |
| Mississippi, signed 2023, no late charge on that installment | 0.00 | 0.00 |

(The rows are hypothetical contracts.)

The credit-capped states carry no date condition: a Tennessee contract of any contract date has its late charges taken up to 5.00.
